title: Sticky Buns

items.raw: 1 cup (240 g) whole milk, warmed to about 105°F
¾ cup (165 g) packed light brown sugar
3 tablespoons (60 g) honey or light corn syrup
1¼ cups (140 g) pecans, toasted and roughly chopped
4 tablespoons (56 g) unsalted butter, very soft
½ cup (110 g) packed brown sugar mixed with 1 tablespoon cinnamon

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Add the warm milk and eggs and mix to a shaggy dough, then knead in the soft butter a piece at a time. Knead 8 to 10 minutes (6 with a dough hook) until smooth and soft. Cover and let rise 1 to 1½ hours, until doubled.
Melt the brown sugar, butter, honey, cream, and salt together in a saucepan, stirring, and bring just to a boil. Pour into a buttered 9×13-inch pan and scatter the pecans over it.
Roll the dough on a lightly floured surface into an 18×12-inch rectangle. Spread with the soft butter, leaving a 1-inch strip bare along one long edge, and sprinkle evenly with the cinnamon sugar.
Roll up tightly from the long filled side and pinch the seam. Cut into 12 even pieces with a sharp serrated knife or unflavored dental floss. Set them cut side down on the pecans.
Cover and let rise 45 to 60 minutes, until puffy and touching. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until deep golden and the center bun reads 190°F. Set a rimmed sheet pan on the rack below to catch drips.

Let rest 5 minutes — no longer, or the goo sets in the pan. Run a knife around the edge, put a large platter or sheet pan on top, and flip in one confident motion. Scrape any pecans left in the pan onto the buns.

notes.label: Overnight version
notes.text: after shaping, cover and refrigerate up to 16 hours. In the morning, let them sit at room temperature 1 to 1½ hours until puffy, then bake.

notes.label: Careful
notes.text: the hot goo is dangerous. Use oven mitts and flip away from you.

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: best the day they are baked. Rewarm leftovers covered at 300°F for 10 minutes.

notes.label: Without nuts
notes.text: leave the pecans out entirely; the goo works on its own.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — soft yeasted buns baked over brown sugar, butter, and pecans. Who makes these, and when — Christmas morning, birthdays? Tell me if yours have raisins, no nuts, or a cinnamon-roll style filling.
